title: Genesis: plan-review capability to prevent the onboarding-v0 stall classes
body: Drafted in response to three onboarding-v0 stalls (F007/F012/F008) that each burned 3-7 paid volley rounds before an operator split/sharpened by hand. Root causes, all detectable pre-implementation: (1) over-scope = feature spanning >1 surface > one 600s dispatch; (2) exemplar/weak ACs = example instead of invariant, inviting whack-a-mole; (3) silent prereq = undeclared dependency (F012 stale command_validation allowlist). Plus D039's caps-file {} raw-schema hard-stop. Design: Layer-1 deterministic lint (free) + Layer-2 design-review volley (paid, triggered), enforced at pre_lock / edit / pre_dispatch with override-able gates, plus cross-feature-edit detection and actionable config readiness. Each feature is authored single-surface with invariant (not exemplar) ACs and explicit test requirements — dogfooding the lint's own rules; the completion_test requires this plan to pass its own lint. Status: draft (NOT locked). Build deferred until onboarding-v0 closes (no-meta-systems-mid-volley). Threshold calibration corpus = F007/F012/F008.

title: Live F009 reproduction: `quota-caps init` -> dispatch config_required (circular remediation)
body: Concrete evidence for F009 (actionable config readiness). Sequence: operator reset quota_caps.json to {}; `quota-caps init` wrote a valid schema_version:1 file seeding ONLY codex.plus.rolling_5h (cap 48987969 = 1.25x observed 39.19M) + claude rolling_7d (percent_of_plan) + gemini. dispatch-from-plan then BLOCKED with quota_readiness='config_required' and remediation 'run quota-caps init' — i.e. it told the operator to run the exact command that produced the unready state (CIRCULAR). Root cause: the readiness check also requires the codex rolling_7d window, which `quota-caps init` does not seed (observed rolling_7d=780410457). F009 must: (a) make `quota-caps init` seed ALL windows the readiness check requires (5h AND 7d for codex), or (b) make the readiness failure name the SPECIFIC missing window and a non-circular remediation, never point back at the command that just ran. This is real product friction that repeatedly derailed the onboarding-v0 dogfood.

title: Stronger F009 evidence: quota-caps v1/v2 schema split blocks dispatch (4th quota failure this session)
body: Within one session the quota subsystem blocked dispatch FOUR distinct ways, none related to the feature under work: (1) caps {} -> readiness config_required with CIRCULAR remediation (run the init that produced it); (2) `quota-caps init` seeds only codex rolling_5h, so readiness stays config_required (wants 7d too); (3) init-derived 5h cap (49M) always false-trips because the codex tokens_local_proxy reads ~0 at rest but a stuck 1.264e8 in-volley; (4) the caps file became {'schema_version':2,'vendors':{}} and the dispatch readiness/budget loader REJECTS it ('schema_version must be 1, got 2; unknown vendor key vendors') even though quota_caps_loader.py itself documents a v2 vendors{} schema — i.e. two loaders in the same package disagree on schema version. F009 scope must therefore include: a single source-of-truth caps schema (no v1/v2 split between loaders), `quota-caps init` seeding ALL readiness-required windows, non-circular remediation messages, and a pre-flight readiness check that names the exact missing/invalid field. This is overwhelming justification for the plan-review config-readiness feature.

title: Bootstrap correction: F009 must be built operator-style FIRST; lock + harness are both quota-blocked
body: Attempted to lock this plan to begin harness-driven build. Lock is BLOCKED: `dontpanic plan lock` runs a pre-impl sufficiency audit (Goal Governance) that is agent-based and therefore routes through the same broken quota/dispatch path that F009 fixes. So BOTH building-via-harness AND locking-via-gate are blocked by the quota subsystem — the very thing F009 repairs. Corrected sequence (operator-confirmed: fix quota as a blocker-class product bug first): build F009 OPERATOR-STYLE with pure local pytest (no agents, no quota, no lock-gate needed) to reconcile the caps schema and readiness, restoring the dispatch path; THEN lock plan-review + run F001-F008 harness-driven; THEN finish onboarding-v0 (F008 last finding + F013/F009/F011/F010). Precise F009 root cause (durable): quota_caps_loader.load() requires schema_version==1 with TOP-LEVEL vendor keys (v1), but the same module documents a v2 vendors{} shape it does not accept; calibration_loader owns a separate quota_calibration.json; `quota-caps init` seeds only codex rolling_5h (readiness also needs rolling_7d); and the readiness failure's remediation points back at the init that produced it (circular). F009 fix: one canonical caps schema with migration, init seeds all readiness windows, non-circular remediation naming the exact missing field, AND an offline/override path for plan lock so a down agent-path cannot block locking. Note: lock-needs-an-agent is itself a plan-review finding worth folding into F004 (pre-lock gate must degrade gracefully when the agent path is unavailable).

title: Pre-lock refresh against onboarding-v0 close evidence; build minimal slice F001->F002->F003->F007 first
body: Refreshed the draft against the new onboarding-v0 evidence before lock: corpus grew from 3 stalls to ~6 over-scope events (added F009 600s-timeout D055/D056, F016 timeout-of-a-split D063) + F011's pre-dispatch 3-way split (D060) as the working counter-example; calibration now weights SURFACE-COUNT above AC-count (F016 timed out at 5 ACs across 3 surfaces; F015 clean at 4 ACs/1 surface). F009 (config-readiness) expanded to validate ROLE config (D065 Grok-Builder/Codex-Auditor split-brain that blocked plan-close), but the proactive doctor-WARN is deliberately kept OUT of F009 to preserve its single surface — dogfooding this plan's own surface-count rule; doctor-WARN stays a separate small feature/follow-up. Operator decisions: build the MINIMAL high-leverage slice first — F001 lint core -> F002 split proposer -> F003 plan-review CLI -> F007 pre-dispatch sizing gate (F002 pulled in by F003's split-proposal remediation dep), then reassess before F004/F005/F006/F008/F009. The 8 onboarding journey-evidence demonstration runs are sequenced AFTER plan-review (and will exercise these gates).

title: STOP before lock — empty user_journeys is a plan-quality defect; fresh-session authoring runbook
body: Lock attempt refused: goal_type=new_feature needs hand-authored pre-impl sufficiency-findings, and underneath it objective_contract.user_journeys is EMPTY (len 0) — a real authoring defect, NOT just mechanics. Forcing the lock would satisfy mechanics while repeating the onboarding-v0 closeout gap (D065). Operator decision: do NOT force the lock; author journeys in a fresh, clean context. FRESH-SESSION RUNBOOK: (1) start from this committed plan-review refresh (branch feat/onboarding-v0-signed-off-finalizer); (2) author concrete objective_contract.user_journeys BEFORE any lock attempt; (3) write pre-impl sufficiency findings against those journeys; (4) lock; (5) dispatch only the first slice F001->F002->F003->F007 with explicit budget. REQUIRED JOURNEY (operator-specified, encodes the D065 lesson so journey-evidence is never an afterthought again): "As an operator closing a plan, I can see whether each required journey has captured evidence before the goal-completion audit runs." Refresh content already landed: corpus 3->~6 over-scope events + F011 pre-split counter-example, surface-count-weighted calibration, F009 role-config expansion (doctor-WARN kept out to stay single-surface). See D005.

title: Journeys authored as structured objects + J6 deferred; plan LOCKED (draft->active)
body: Resolved D006. Root cause of the 'user_journeys EMPTY (len 0)' report: the 5 journeys were authored as PLAIN STRINGS, but ObjectiveContract.user_journeys requires structured UserJourney objects (name + description>=10 + optional surfaces/states/acceptance_signals, extra=forbid); strings fail model_validate, so the effective parsed count was 0. Fix: rewrote all 5 as structured objects (plan-review-report, pre-lock-design-gate, mid-dev-scope-delta [folds F006+F008], pre-dispatch-sizing-gate, config-readiness-preflight) each mapped to features, plus the D006-required 6th journey close-time-journey-evidence (the D065 lesson). J6 DISPOSITION (operator-chosen via AskUserQuestion): DEFER to a follow-up plan, NOT add F010 here, to preserve the plan's single-surface thesis (mirrors the doctor-WARN deferral in D005). Encoded as: (a) journey recorded in the contract; (b) one hand-authored pre-impl sufficiency finding (journey_id=close-time-journey-evidence, gap_class=missing_feature, severity=low/non-blocking, feature_refs=[]) recommending a follow-up plan; (c) an explicit non_goals entry. Hand-authored sufficiency-findings.json under evidence/goal-governance/pre_impl/ per D006 (the agent-based sufficiency auditor routes through the quota/dispatch path F009 repairs, so it was NOT run; lock_plan only CONSUMES the findings file, so the hand-authored path bypasses the quota block). `dontpanic plan lock` passed external_refs + requires_capabilities + sufficiency gate and flipped status draft->active with NO override needed. Added the required `## Target` section (target_env:dev, target_project:none) that the advisory sidecars expect. NEXT: dispatch first slice F001->F002->F003->F007 only under explicit operator budget (per D005/D006 runbook); not started this session.

title: F001 dispatched, stalled no-progress, operator-resolved (F2 fixed; F1 stale-report; F3 interpretive)
body: Dispatched F001 via dontpanic dispatch-from-plan --confirm (claude impl / codex aud, quota ok 13%/63%, unrelated-dirty-state acknowledged). Volley hit stopped_no_progress after 2 rounds (verdict unchanged, taxonomy=implementation_defect). Empirical replay of codex's 3 findings against the produced code: (F1 missing_prereq plain-text command tokens) ALREADY RESOLVED in implementer i1 (extract_named_tokens('... --format') returns [('--format','flag')]); codex i1 re-reported it stale -> classify stale-report/talking-past, no action. (F2 weak-test misses 'string matches expected'/'matches the expected') GENUINE feature_defect: _EQUALITY_RE covered 'matches the string' but not those phrasings; the implementer i1 mis-addressed an exemplar pattern instead (finding-number mismatch). OPERATOR FIX: extended _EQUALITY_RE with '\bstring matches\b|\bmatches (?:the )?expected\b' + 2 tests (positive phrasings + property-redemption negative). (F3 role-name surface false-positive) MITIGATED/interpretive: current code produces only a single 'orchestration' surface tag, NO over_surface flag (the feared false-positive does not reproduce); tagging role-config as orchestration is defensible -> non-blocking, no change. Result: 27/27 targeted tests green; F001 flipped passes:true as operator_resolved. This stall (impl+auditor talking past each other on finding numbering + one real 1-line gap) is exactly the convergence-failure class the plan-review feature itself targets — useful dogfood signal. NEXT: F002 -> F003 -> F007 under explicit budget.

title: F002 split proposer: latched-breaker friction + operator-resolved (F1 multi-surface-AC honesty; F2 ruff)
body: F002 dispatch FIRST paused at 0 rounds on a LATCHED breaker:no_progress inherited from F001's stall (plan-scoped gate-state, cleared_gates=[], active_breakers=['breaker:no_progress']). Cleared via `dontpanic approve <plan> breaker:no_progress` (no tokens spent) and re-dispatched. FRICTION worth a follow-up: a feature-scoped no_progress breaker latches at PLAN scope and blocks the NEXT feature's first dispatch until manually approved — a stale-gate papercut (relates to harness-volley-frictions gate-state reconciliation work). Re-dispatch then hit stopped_no_progress after 2 rounds (taxonomy=unknown). Empirical reconciliation of codex's 2 findings: (F1 high/correctness: a single multi-surface AC routed to a single-surface child, violating acceptance #2) GENUINE — operator fix: child.surfaces now reflects the union of its ACs' tags (honest, not silently single), propose_split records offending ACs on new SplitProposal.multi_surface_acs advisory, and the conservation guard is now an explicit SplitConservationError raise (not bare assert). (F2 medium/style: ruff S101 production assert + B905 zip without strict) GENUINE+confirmed — fixed (assert->raise; zip strict=False). 41/41 targeted tests green (27 F001 + 14 F002 incl. 2 new multi-surface-AC tests); ruff clean on split.py + test. F002 flipped passes:true operator_resolved. Second consecutive 2-round stall needing operator-finish — pattern: thorough cross-vendor auditor on small single-surface features always finds 1-3 nits, implementer can't flip codex to signed_off within the 2-round no_progress window. Not a harness bug; operator-finish is the pragmatic close. NEXT: F003 (plan-review CLI) -> F007 under explicit budget.

title: Two follow-ups from the F001/F002 convergence pattern (do NOT block the slice)
body: Operator direction after F001+F002 both closed via operator-finish on 2-round stopped_no_progress: the pattern is worth recording but must NOT stop the slice. Two follow-ups reinforced: (1) the no_progress breaker may be too BLUNT for small-feature audit convergence — when each round produces a DISTINCT small fix (verdict stays needs_changes but the findings shrink/change), 'verdict unchanged across 2 rounds' fires even though real progress is happening; consider a findings-delta-aware convergence signal (cf. convergence-bugs-v2 Design B strictly-shrinking carve-out, which only covers shrinking COUNT, not changing content). (2) 'operator-finish after a signed-off-adjacent audit' should become a FIRST-CLASS close path, not an exception hand-done each time (relates to onboarding-v0 D025: no clean no-paid signed_off->passes finalizer). Both are follow-ups for a future plan; F003 proceeds now. Also re-affirmed: same-plan parallel dispatch is NOT supported (plan-scoped gate-state + plan-wide no_progress breaker); cross-plan fleet scheduling is the parallelism axis. F003 scoped to the plan-review CLI ONLY — must not absorb F007 gate behavior.

title: F003 plan-review CLI: cleanest close — sole finding was untracked-files staging artifact (signed-off-adjacent)
body: F003 dispatched (after pre-clearing the relatched breaker:no_progress again — third occurrence, see D010). 2-round stopped_no_progress, but codex's SOLE finding was high/correctness 'required F003 files (report.py, test_plan_review_cli_f003.py) are untracked and would be omitted from a tracked-diff commit' — NOT a code defect; a pure staging artifact resolved by the close commit's git add (this is the textbook 'operator-finish after signed-off-adjacent audit' case from D010 follow-up #2). Verification: both files exist; the implementer also added the `plan-review` subcommand to command_validation.py allowlist + test (correctly honoring the F012 silent-prereq lesson); 52 plan-review tests (F001+F002+F003 CLI) + 81 command_validation tests pass; ruff clean on report.py/lint.py/__init__/cli test; `dontpanic plan-review <plan>` smoke runs, renders text report, exit-codes on BLOCK. No code change needed for close. F003 flipped passes:true. DOGFOOD SIGNAL (not an F003 defect, tracked for the plan-level completion_test): running plan-review on its OWN plan yields 27 block-severity flags incl. false-positive missing_prereq on symbols the features merely DESCRIBE (lint_feature, over_surface, propose_split...) because the CLI's resolver set isn't wired to the plan's own declared symbols. The completion_test requires the plan to pass its own lint with no block flags — that needs F001 calibration + self-lint resolver wiring (F009/completion territory), NOT F003. NEXT: F007 (pre-dispatch sizing gate) under explicit budget; pre-clear breaker first.

title: F007 pre-dispatch sizing gate: codex SIGNED_OFF (0 findings) — blocked only on patch-completeness (untracked files); minimal slice COMPLETE
body: F007 (after pre-clearing breaker — 4th time) ran ONE round: codex verdict signed_off with ZERO findings — the first clean auditor signoff of the slice. Terminal was 'blocked' (NOT stopped_no_progress): supervisor raised PatchCompletenessError at post_iter because the new test file was untracked. Adds plan_review/sizing_gate.py (evaluate_feature + render_preflight, reuses F001 lint) + wires a pre-dispatch sizing gate + --allow-oversize override into dispatch-from-plan (cli.py) + 8 tests. Verification: 8 F007 tests pass; full slice regression green; F007's own code (sizing_gate.py, the cli.py diff, the test) is ruff-CLEAN. Resolution = stage the files (sizing_gate.py + test + cli.py + __init__.py); NO code change needed. Closed as a genuine signoff (NOT via `dontpanic close --operator-resolved`, which would mischaracterize a clean signoff as a no-progress operator-judgment close). TWO findings-for-followup (refine D010): (1) the patch-completeness gate flagged the untracked TEST file but NOT the untracked MODULE sizing_gate.py — incomplete untracked-file detection (a real gap, the module import would also break a fresh clone). (2) `dontpanic close --operator-resolved` is scoped to stopped_no_progress + requires breaker:no_progress active — it does NOT cover the 'auditor signed_off but patch-completeness blocked on untracked files' case; the first-class operator-finish path (D010 follow-up #2) has this coverage gap. OUT OF SCOPE / pre-existing (noted, not fixed): cli.py carries 3 ruff errors (S105 drift_token, S603 subprocess, S101 assert) present at HEAD in the config-handler region, unrelated to F007. SELF-REFERENTIAL NOTE: F007's gate now lives in dispatch-from-plan; since plan-review's own features lint as over_surface (F003 dogfood), dispatching further features (F004/F005/F006/F008/F009) may now be blocked by F007's gate and need --allow-oversize. MINIMAL SLICE F001->F002->F003->F007 COMPLETE (4/9 features). NEXT: D005 reassessment — continue to F004/F005/F006/F008/F009 or pause.
